item.text: {"question_id":"8B.5","answer":"During 2023, the administration established formal coordination and control mechanisms across some federal programs. The National Public Security Program made implementation mandatory for federal agencies, assigned monitoring to security, finance, and public-administration ministries, and required budget-funded execution and oversight (BATCH-0044-E011). IMSS-BIENESTAR prescribed central, regional, hospital, and zonal supervision, written commitments, multidisciplinary visits, corrective measures, information systems, and interinstitutional coordination; however, these were formal rules rather than demonstrated effectiveness (BATCH-0051-E002; BATCH-0051-E004). The UN reported structured coordination with federal, state, municipal, civil-society, private, and international actors during the Otis response, but this was substantially partner-supported and does not establish the president’s personal direction or the adequacy of the overall response (BATCH-0015-E015; BATCH-0015-E018). There is also evidence of reach in selected programs: the adult pension expanded to 10.8 million beneficiaries by 2022, and ten of fourteen programs with coverage indicators exceeded their planned absolute coverage targets using definitive 2022 data. These figures do not establish uniform compliance, service quality, or 2023 milestone completion, and two programs lacked coverage indicators (BATCH-0032-E006; BATCH-0052-E005). Against this, coordination and follow-through were materially uneven. CONEVAL found that four priority programs did not measure results, eight required work on result measurement or indicators, half required stronger logical association between components and objectives, and monitoring recommendations had been disregarded to varying degrees (BATCH-0052-E004; BATCH-0052-E006). Social programs showed information, training, monitoring, payment, communication, and access problems, including deficient follow-up and conflicts among implementers (BATCH-0018-E006). CNDH found inconsistent protocols, incomplete records, staffing and capacity gaps, large federal-state data discrepancies, and no uniform guarantee of multidisciplinary implementation in migrant-child protection (BATCH-0015-E007). The Ayotzinapa investigation documented institutional concealment or denial of records, noncompliance with presidential information requests, withdrawn warrants, turnover, delays, and continuing fragmentation, despite recognized advances by one investigative team (BATCH-0013-E002; BATCH-0013-E003). Security reach likewise did not ensure integrated civilian compliance: military institutions dominated spending, local security transfers declined, the Guard remained overwhelmingly military and incompletely certified, while WOLA reported detention under-registration and inadequate civilian controls (BATCH-0016-E007; BATCH-0009-E003). Major project execution further showed weak milestone discipline: Maya Train design changes, permit and environmental-process disputes, partial opening, delays, cost escalation, incomplete track, uncertain costs, and unresolved transfer and expenditure documentation (BATCH-0011-E007; BATCH-0030-E004; BATCH-0040-E008). Overall, the supplied evidence supports substantial top-down reach and formal coordination in selected domains, but mixed and often weak horizontal coordination, monitoring, compliance, documentation, and milestone completion across the broader system. Presidential attribution is strongest for the governing architecture, priorities, and major projects; actual implementation also depended on subordinate agencies, other levels of government, external partners, and institutional constraints. it demonstrates institutional noncompliance and delay without proving López Obrador personally ordered concealment.","World Bank and UN evidence covers particular partnerships or responses, not the whole Mexican state.","External shocks, institutional turnover, intergovernmental authority, subordinate resistance, and partner contributions limit causal attribution."],"corrections_made":["Removed the unsupported implication that national reach, coverage, or target exceedance established broad coordination, uniform compliance, service quality, or milestone completion.","Qualified Otis coordination and social-program reach as joint or externally supported activity rather than direct presidential achievement.","Added CONEVAL evidence on weak result orientation, absent or inadequate measurement, weak logical association, and disregarded monitoring recommendations.","Retained and sharpened contrary evidence on institutional noncompliance, incomplete records, staffing and protocol gaps, appointment delays, project incompletion, and audit or transfer irregularities.","Separated formal architecture and presidential priorities from actual implementation by subordinate agencies, other governments, partners, and institutional constraints.","Preserved the 2023 period while explicitly identifying when evidence reflects 2022 baselines or inherited conditions."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A complete portfolio-wide ledger of milestones, territorial compliance, and cross-ministry coordination is not supplied.","Further review could distinguish presidentially controlled implementation from agency, state, municipal, military, donor, and civil-society execution.","The effect of formal supervision mechanisms on actual 2023 service delivery and compliance remains insufficiently observed."]}
